title: Starter kits and smoke harness for third-party adapters
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This document provides lightweight, production-minded starter kits and a smoke-test harness for onboarding third-party adapter integrations (client adapters, proxy adapters, and partner-hosted connectors) into the Redwood developer experience. It is intended for SDK maintainers, integrators, and on-call engineers who need a repeatable, low-friction path to validate compatibility, telemetry, and error-handling before broad rollout.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-green for new adapter integrations by providing reusable templates.
- Catch common integration breakages early (serialization, streaming, auth, timeouts).
- Standardize CI/edge gating for third-party code paths.

Scope and when to use this guide:
- Use for: new third-party adapter onboarding, patch releases of adapters, and pre-release validation for SDK changes that affect adapters.
- Not for: in-depth performance benchmarking or long-running production load tests (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).

Fast summary of components included:
- smoke-harness/ : minimal harness to run local and CI smoke checks (node and python examples).
- conformance-check/ : deterministic contract checks for API surface (response shape, error codes, headers).
- ci-templates/ : GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates that run the harness and publish a pass/fail artifact.

Prerequisites:
1) SDK repo or adapter source checked out.
2) API key with dev scope (REDD-DEV-KEY or equivalent) available in CI.
3) Small sample dataset (included in /samples) with 6–10 representative prompts.

Quickstart: run the local smoke harness (node)
1) Install: npm ci
2) Configure: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDWOOD_DEV_KEY
3) Run: npm run smoke -- --adapter ./adapters/thirdparty/http-adapter.js

What the smoke harness validates (default checks):
- Happy-path generation: token stream completes without error.
- Streaming reconnection: simulated mid-stream disconnect and retry.
- Auth failure handling: 401 -> falls back to configured retry policy.
- Response schema: top-level keys match expectations (chunk.id, chunk.text, meta.latency_ms).
- Telemetry hooks: trace/span created and service.name tag set to adapter.<adapter-name>.

Example output (pass):
- SUMMARY: 6 tests run, 0 failures, 1 warning (latency > 300ms)

Conformance check example (YAML config table):
| key | description | required | example |
|-----|-------------|----------|---------|
| adapter_name | Unique adapter id used in routing | yes | http-adapter-3p |
| base_url | Upstream service endpoint (can be mocked) | yes | https://api.partner.example/v1 |
| auth_scheme | one of [bearer, hmac, mtls] | yes | bearer |
| health_endpoint | path used for liveness probe | no | /healthz |
| max_concurrent_requests | safety throttle for local harness | no | 8 |

Example conformance CLI (python):
$ python -m redwood_adapter_checks.run --config ci-templates/thirdparty-config.yaml --samples samples/small-suite.json

CI templates (recommended GitHub Actions snippet):
- name: Adapter smoke checks
  uses: actions/checkout@v3
- name: Setup Node
  uses: actions/setup-node@v4
- name: Install and run smoke harness
  run: |
    npm ci
    export REDWOOD_API_KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_DEV_KEY }}
    npm run smoke -- --adapter ./adapters/${{ matrix.adapter }} --output smoke-results.json
- name: Upload results
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: smoke-results-${{ matrix.adapter }}
    path: smoke-results.json

Failure modes and canonical fixes (top support issues):
1) Symptom: intermittent streaming disconnects from partners (partial tokens, ECONNRESET).
   Canonical fix: ensure harness uses TCP keepalive and the adapter implements idempotent resume tokens (see section "Streaming resilience patterns"). Also add exponential-backoff jitter and client-side reconnection limit of 3.
2) Symptom: schema mismatch errors in prod only (unexpected top-level fields).
   Canonical fix: add a schema-validation step in conformance-check and bump schema version in adapter registry. Create a canary rollout with header X-Adp-Compat: v2.
3) Symptom: CI passes locally but fails in GH Actions due to auth scope errors.
   Canonical fix: verify secret permissions, ensure token is scoped for the test org, and use short-lived tokens if the partner requires IP allowlisting; when IP allowlisting exists, run remote harness inside a dev VPC.

Streaming resilience patterns (recommended):
- Always attach an idempotency token to persistent streams.
- Emit periodic checkpoints (every 512 tokens) so downstream can resume.
- For partial responses, return structured "resume_after" metadata.

Template snippets: sample adapter conftest.py (pytest)
---
def test_adapter_health(adapter_client):
    resp = adapter_client.get('/healthz')
    assert resp.status_code in (200, 204)
---

Ownership and runbook (who does what):
- Adapter author: supplies adapter package, config schema, and sample traffic.
- SDK integration owner (team SDK-DX): maintains harness templates and CI snippets.
- On-call: triages fails flagged by the CI gate.

Runbook: CI fails with non-zero smoke harness exit code
1) Check artifact smoke-results.json for first failing test and the recorded stack trace.
2) If failure is network-level (ECONN*), re-run with partner mock enabled; if it recurs, open a SRE ticket and tag adapter-owner.
3) If failure is schema-related, open a minor incident, block rollout, and notify product and legal if the adapter modifies data residency behavior.

Rollout checklist for a new adapter (pre-prod -> prod):
1) Local harness: 100% pass on the small sample suite.
2) CI: smoke checks pass and artifact uploaded.
3) Conformance: contract checks against staging upstream.
4) Canary: 1% traffic for 24 hours with tracing enabled.
5) Ramp: 5%, 25%, 100% with automated rollback on error budget violation > 5%.

Troubleshooting quick reference:
- 401 during CI only: check token scopes and repo-level secrets.
- High latency warnings: compare partner latency to historical baseline and set temporary rate limit.
- Missing telemetry tags: ensure SDK-level trace wrapper calls adapter.register_trace() in initialization.

FAQ:
Q: Can I use the harness for long-running performance tests?
A: No — harness is intentionally lightweight. Use eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite for load testing.

Q: How do I add a new language binding?
A: Add a language adapter folder in smoke-harness/lang/ with the required adapter_runner.sh and a CI matrix entry. See the CI template section above.
